paragraphs.text: Native DeepSeek Harness bundle for gitfeed: RSS reader page, refresh schedule, git sync, agent tool.
Code only; data lives in a separate repository.
# gitfeed-native

A personal RSS reader rendered as a **native DeepSeek Harness plugin**: a reader
page in the right S

idebar (beside Files) and in the main panel, a Host-side
job runner for feed refresh and read-state

sync, and one compact
`gitfeed` agent tool.

The package is **code only**. The data it reads lives in a separate repository,
so installing, updat

ing, and sharing the plugin never touches subscriptions,
items, or read state — it writes nothing in

to that repository and asks for no
token. Fetching happens where the reader runs, on the Host's own

job runner;
there is no server-side job to arm.
## What it looks like

The panel: folders on the left, one line per item with its digest, and the
article beside them. A fe

ed row carries its own actions — move it to a folder,
mark the source read, unsubscribe — and the st

ar sits on the item row, so
keeping something does not mean opening it first.
The same reader in the right Sidebar, beside whatever session is open:

Moving a source lists the folders already in use, marks the one it is in, and
keeps naming a new one

lists the folders already in use, marks the one it is in, and
keeps naming a new one on its own row:

The library in those images is a fixture (`docs/screenshots/demo-library.js`),
not a real reading li

st: it answers the reader's own API with invented
subscriptions and items, so no one's feeds or hist
ory are in this repository.
## Two repositories, one reader
| repository | contents | visibility |
| `zizon/gitfeed-native` (this one) | the plugin: TypeScript sources, bundle metadata, CLI | public

|
| `zizon/gitfeed` | the reader data: `feeds.json`, `config.json`, `data/` | private, cloned to `~/
/gitfeed` | the reader data: `feeds.json`, `config.json`, `data/` | private, cloned to `~/gitfeed` |
Why split them:

- **The code can be public, the reading cannot.** Installing from GitHub means
the plugin repository

is readable by anyone. Subscriptions, fetched items,
and read/star ids belong to the person reading

them, so they stay in a
repository that person owns. The data repository can stay private forever.

- **Updates stop colliding with data commits.** `git pull` for code and
`git pull` for read state ar

e now different repositories, so a plugin upgrade
can never rebase your reading list.
- **The data i

s portable.** The plugin's default `repo` is `~/gitfeed`; cloning
your data repository there is the

whole setup. Nothing about the plugin pins
a machine or a user.

The plugin still dogfoods: this checkout is developed against the real data
repository, and the CLI

in this package runs the same `lib/host` fetcher the
reader uses.
## Quick start

1. Clone the data repository to `~/gitfeed` (or let the plugin write a starter
root on first activat

ion).
2. Install the bundle (see **Install**).
3. Open the **Feeds** card, subscribe, **Fetch**, rea

d. If the root is a
checkout, **Sync** pushes subscriptions and read state.

Each item row shows the title, its feed and age, and a one-line plain-text
digest of the summary, so

a list can be skimmed and skipped without opening
every article. Display prefs turn the digest off

(rows then use the shorter
two-line height); the choice is stored per browser.

Both actions a reader wants *while reading a feed* live on that feed's section
row in the list: `Ope

n Source Security  [Unsubscribe] [Mark 16 read]`. The
section header sticks to the top while its sec

tion is in view, so they are at
hand whenever a post from that feed is on screen; `Unsubscribe` firs

t swaps the
row into a confirm (`Cancel` / `Unsubscribe`) and only then removes the
subscription and

that feed's items. A folder section can only be marked.
The Feeds panel keeps the same two marks on

a feed's own row, which is how a
feed is managed without opening it, and no row shows a count twice

a feed's own row, which is how a
feed is managed without opening it, and no row shows a count twice.

A single selected source is marked from its own row, so the floating bar speaks
only for a wider vie

w: an active search (`Mark results read`) or the whole
library (`Mark all read`). Its ▾ appears only

when the other of those two
exists, and the library-wide entry needs a second, differently placed c

lick.
The toast that follows carries **Undo**. No key marks in bulk.

Background refresh: the rail's second bar ends with the age of the last run
(`2m`; it shows `…` whil

e a run is in flight and the Fetch button spins then).
The ⋯ menu's **Refresh** block shows the inte

rval and the last result
(`0 new · 35 failed`), and its **Sync** block shows the auto-sync interval,

the next run, and the last result. The main page's status line carries the
refresh interval beside
the branch, with the same detail in its tooltip.
## Where it lives in the Harness UI
| surface | how to reach it |
| Right Sidebar page | the RSS button in the conversation header, or the **Feeds** card in the right

Sidebar's **+** guide. It sits beside Files, Documents, Terminals, and Plans. |
| Main panel page |
the gitfeed icon in the left Sidebar's global panel rail (beside Plugins and Tasks). This view also

works without a session. |
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- **Only what the feed gives you.** Some feeds publish a teaser; "Open
original" is one click away.

- **Not offline.** Images are hotlinked from the origin.
- **Fetching needs a fetcher somewhere.** T

he Host does it while it runs, and a
cron entry on an always-on machine covers the rest. If nothing

is running,
items wait.
- **Loopback only.** The API is served by the Harness web server and refuses

cross-origin requests; it is not designed to be exposed publicly.
- **The reader needs its Host's e

vent stream.** There is no polling fallback: a
page refreshed before a Host restart cannot load, and

a proxy that buffers
`text/event-stream` breaks it. Update and restart together.
- **The right Side

bar needs a session.** The main-panel page works without one.
- **Item history is pruned** to `fetch

.keepMonths` (6) to keep the data repo
small.
- **Feed health is manual.** Dead feeds show red in th

e rail and in
`data/meta.json`; nothing emails you.
- **The installed copy is a build artifact.** Ed

iting the profile's
`node_modules/gitfeed-native` is overwritten by the next install; edit this
chec

kout and reinstall.
- **The data repository is yours to back up.** Nothing in this package stores
or
uploads the data; a lost data checkout is a lost reading list.
